proof_summary: Take $n=800322180$; monotonicity of $B(k)=\binom{2k+1}{k}$ and $B(16)>n$ force any putative representation to have $c,d\le 15$. A finite factorization check shows that for every such pair, $n-B(c)-B(d)$ contains a prime congruent to $3\pmod 4$ to an odd exponent, so the sum-of-two-squares criterion rules out the remaining two square terms.
